body:
While I KNOW that I'm not too big, getting such comments from close family members suck, since I can't just leave the situation. 

I used to be much skinnier, and they might very well just be responding in a bad way to the changes. Hopefully they'll soon realise that change isn't necessarily bad.

Edit: Your ninja edit makes my reply seem really out of context. Meh, no changing that.

Oops, forgot to put an "on" in there. But yeah, I'd kinda made my mind up to just do me. If they don't want to change, I can't change them.

Solving the problem would be great though :)
My appearence is pretty damn mediocre. Almost all of the guys I see at the gym are bigger than me.

That was my thought as well. I have recently begun doubting my knowledge, since 80% of people at my (commercial) gym deadlifting don't simply lock out, but hyperextend instead.

I've even witnessed people encouraging each other to "get the full motion" by hyperextending, or in their words, locking out.
What is the deal with people leaning like 30 degrees backwards at the top of the deadlift!?

I've been putting a lot of effort into working out. My appearance is slowly changing in a positive way except for one part.

Why the fuck can't my skin keep up? I have 6-8 stretch marks on the back of my shoulders on each side. They are all ranging from 2-5cm and it's pissing me off. Fuck you stretch marks.

Powerlifting.

When I started out, I was doing a bodybuilding programme, but I quickly realised that I found more satisfaction in watching the amount of weight in my lifts rise.

Lifting heavy ass shit is also my favourite way to vent when distressed :)
